newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen futures capped despite JGB gains.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen futures capped despite JGB gains.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures failed to make much headway on Monday even as Japanese government bond (JGB) futures hit new highs on short-covering by hedge funds.
"Market sentiment has swung around once again. There's no rate hike expected at least till the autumn now," said a dealer with a European futures house.

He said the Nikkei's failure to attract any real fund flows at the start of the new Japanese financial year and with the Bank of Japan's quarterly tankan survey out of the way was also boosting the performance of bond futures.
June JGBs soared to a high of 127.28 before coming off slightly to settle at 127.17 against their previous 126.96.
"The hedge funds that are short are going to have to cut their positions. Now we're through here, they know 128.00 is coming sooner or later," the dealer said.
He said activity was driven mainly by hedge funds with little interest from Japanese domestic players on Monday.
"I suspect we'd see more short-covering if there are any dips back towards 127.00," he said.
December Euroyen stood at 99.16 at 1140 GMT after hitting a high of 99.18 against its IMM close at 99.17.
"It'll struggle to get much above 99.20 unless we see some fresh data showing growth slowing in the second quarter," the dealer said.

Eurodollar futures ended slightly higher after coming under pressure in Chicago on Friday following the release of the U.S. jobs report for March, which showed a drop in the unemployment rate and an increase in average hourly earnings.
The data fuelled speculation of another U.S. rate hike by May. Dealers said the market would keep a close watch on U.S. retail sales data for March, due on Friday.
December Eurodollars finished at 93.415 against their IMM close at 93.400 on light volume of 5,705 lots.
